newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude outlook - fuzzy on prods, technicals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude outlook - fuzzy on prods, technicals.

text.p: The outlook for U.S. crude prices looks fuzzy this week, although refined products and technical factors are likely to continue weighing down on the market, analysts said on Monday.

The market fuzziness reflects the gradual changeover from winter into spring, when the influence of heating oil is beginning to fade but gasoline still hasn't taken over as a dominant market factor, analysts said.

"There really is no news out there at all. It's more technical than anything else," said Tom Bentz, an analyst with ING Derivatives in New York. "Weather is less and less of a factor, and people have written off heating oil."
Bentz and other analysts peg support for crude at last week's low of $23.63 a barrel.
March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading around $24.20-30 a barrel at midday on Monday, up 10 cents from late Friday's cash market.

But not all analysts have discarded the role of heating oil. John Saucer, an analyst with Smith Barney in New York, is still looking to the winter fuel and other products for overall market direction.
"Heating oil is very vulnerable right now," said Saucer. March heating oil was trading around 65.55-65 cents a gallon at midday, with support estimated at 65.25 cents.
And despite warmer-than-normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast this week, the weather could still pull some surprises before spring sets in.
Meteorologists said Monday that the eastern United States could be hit by an Arctic blast next week, with freezing temperatures possibly as far south as Florida.
